title: Garage or car repair

fields.label: Jobs and prices
fields.help: MOT or inspections, servicing, brakes, tyres, air-con, diagnostics: prices for small, medium and large cars (or vans), as you charge them.

fields.label: What you work on
fields.help: Cars, SUVs, vans, a make you specialise in.

fields.label: Guarantees and how you work
fields.help: Warranty, photos or videos of what you find, approval before work, courtesy cars, same-day work.

fields.label: Accreditations
fields.help: MOT/inspection station, IMI, ASE, AAA, trade bodies, exactly as they must appear.

fields.label: Opening hours and drop-off
fields.help: Drop-off times, days you're closed, courtesy car or shuttle and what it costs.

fields.label: Brand colour
fields.help: Optional: your sign or overalls colour. It sits on a dark page, so a bright colour works best.

writerNotes: The hero follows one vehicle through the workshop: booked in, up on the lift, every check marked ok, warn (advised) or bad, the bad one sent to the owner's phone with a price and approved, fixed in a close-up, then road tested and ready. car.body picks the outline (hatch, suv or van): choose what the garage mostly works on. car.reg is a plausible registration in the local format; car.paint any colour.

checks: four to ten from the brief's inspection (tyres, brakes, oil, coolant, battery, lights, wipers, suspension, exhaust, steering; each place once) with short readings (3 mm, 12.6 V, Full). Exactly one is bad: make it a common job from the brief's price list and write fix.what and fix.price (with the currency) to match. Use the local spelling (tyres or tires) in checks.*.n.

Write the six stages for that vehicle and that fault, with clock times through one working day. labels are the words drawn in the bay: the bay name, the ready line, and approve, approved and new in the local language.

prices.sizes: two to four sizes of vehicle with local example models and a shape (small, medium, large, van). prices.jobs: the brief's jobs with a price for every size, in the same order (repeat a fixed price for every size). prices.start: the size and up to four jobs ticked at first.

promise: up to three of the brief's promises with a short key (12 mo, Photos, Same day). promise.ask is the sample message: the same fault as the hero with its price, plus up to two advised items. creds: only the accreditations the brief gives, exactly; never invent one.

book: drop-off times, closed days (0 Sunday to 6 Saturday), up to four options while the vehicle is in with their price or Free, plate (uk for UK registrations, otherwise plain) and the local word for the registration. The booking form really sends: the request goes to the garage, who confirm it. Never say it is booked, paid or confirmed.

hero.title and hero.titleEm: a short two-part headline (four lines at most on a desktop, set in capitals). theme.accent is the garage's colour on a dark page: bright enough for dark button text; theme.wordmarkFit is always "fit".
business.name is set to exactly the name in the brief and cannot be changed; brand.name is how it appears in the nav and the footer (short).
